mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding near-term expected cash flows.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, no significant negative returns occur after such Fed rate spikes (t-test p > 0.05); or the 20-day return is not statistically different from the prior month's return (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 3.5% for two consecutive months coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as lower labor market participation and tighter wage growth reduce recession risk.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises above 3.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes with high inflation, the 20-day return is not statistically positive after such UNRATE increases (p > 0.10); or the effect is not detectable in a 60-day horizon (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDP demand (GDPC1) grows at a double-digit pace for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive as market anticipates robust corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly growth > +10% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day return occurs after such GDP demand spikes in periods of high inflation or high interest rates (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) index below 105 for four consecutive months predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals weakening manufacturing capacity and potential supply shocks.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 105 for four consecutive months
regime_hint: Supply-side contraction in a growth cycle
failure_condition: Over 12 such contraction months, the 60-day forward returns are not consistently negative (median p-value > 0.25 across windows).

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation index exceeds 4% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative as investors anticipate rate hikes that compress equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 4% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In a 60-day window, no negative returns occur after such CPI spikes when the Fed rate remains unchanged (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in monthly employment (PAYEMS) below 150,000 coincides with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates a potential recession and risk-asset flight to quality.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls below 150,000 in a single month
failure_condition: Over 10 such months, the 5-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.10) or the effect is not robust to lagged variables (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rises in both HOUST (housing starts) and RSAFS (residential investment) by more than 10% in the same month produce a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals renewed housing-driven economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > +10% AND RSAFS increases > +10% in the same month
failure_condition: In 20 such interaction events, the 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.10) or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a 'late-cycle expansion' as judged by a combination of low unemployment (UNRATE < 4%) and high industrial production (INDPRO > 110) is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as markets anticipate a prolonged economic upswing.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% AND INDPRO > 110 for at least 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: During such regimes, the 60-day forward return is not significantly positive (median p-value > 0.25 across multiple cycles).
